transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-09-06
- Time: 14:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Hsu (Redwood SE), Anita Gomez (CTO, Starlight), Samir Patel (SRE Lead, Starlight), Priya Nair (PM, Starlight)

Summary:
Quick onboarding/runway kickoff focused on networking and access handoff for staging, pilot scope (inference workloads), and initial security checklist. Mostly technical clarifications around VPC peering, SSO/SAML mapping, KMS for keys, and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for predictable throughput. Agreed to run a staging network test and for Redwood to share runbook and pricing for a small Dedicated pilot.

Topics covered:
- Staging network and VPC peering
- SSO & RBAC mapping
- KMS / data residency concerns
- Pilot sizing and Dedicated vs Hosted economics
- Observability and runbook for failure modes / fallback

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — we have Marcus from SE — 
[00:03] Marcus Hsu: hey, hi. good to meet y'all.
[00:06] Anita Gomez: Hi! Anita here. we'll take notes.
[00:09] Samir Patel: Samir on SRE team. been looking at the network diagrams you sent. couple questions.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Priya here — product. excited to get this rolling.

[02:10] Lena Park: Cool. agenda — primarily we want to hand off the staging/network access, confirm pilot scope (latency SLOs, throughput), and align on security artifacts. Marcus will walk through the staging checklist and what we need for VPC peering.

[04:05] Marcus Hsu: quick note, our staging workflow expects either VPC peering or private link; peering is usually simpler for customers doing full egress control. For the pilot, we recommend a small Dedicated pool if you want predictable throughput — otherwise hosted with pinned routes can work but you'll see more latency variance.

[06:12] Samir Patel: When you say Dedicated pool, is that a per-tenant GPU pool or multi-tenant? what are the guarantees?

[06:45] Lena Park: Dedicated is reserved capacity — per-customer pool, SLA-backed. guarantees on throughput and lower tail latency. for pilot we can do a small commit, burst allowed, and scale with a short notice. We'll send the exact commit tiers in the pricing doc.

[08:02] Anita Gomez: our main worry is cost vs latency. our use-case is live support routing — 99th percentile latency under 150ms ideally, but we need to balance with run-rate cost.

[08:45] Marcus Hsu: yeah that's a common tradeoff. two levers — batching and prefix/KV caching — those reduce tokens and cost but can add a bit to p50 in some cases. Also quantized variants can lower spend with small quality delta. We'll propose a config for your workload.

[11:30] Priya Nair: on quality — we have some prompt sets and evals, we can share. we want to avoid regressions during model rollouts.

[12:05] Lena Park: perfect, include those. Redwood Optimize will flag regressions if model changes alter eval scores. we can wire alerts.

[13:40] Samir Patel: let's talk networking specifics — CIDRs, NAT, and bastion requirements. we can't open inbound from public into our staging; we prefer peering plus a managed bastion.

[14:12] Marcus Hsu: understood. for peering we'll need the VPC CIDR and a thumbs-up on route tables. we support a tight egress ACL set. bastion is fine for ops; we also support a managed connector for SSH tunnels.

[16:20] Samir Patel: what about audit logs and retention? we have compliance to keep request-level logs for 365 days but redacted PII. can you support that?

[16:40] Lena Park: Yes — we have an observability retention add-on and can configure for log retention. for PII we do redaction at ingestion or you can route to your KMS-managed S3. We'll put the SOC2 docs and log configuration examples in the runbook.

[18:55] Anita Gomez: KMS, right — do you support customer-managed keys? our security team insists.

[19:12] Marcus Hsu: yep, CMKs via KMS/HSM is supported in the Private offering and in Dedicated with KMS integration. On Hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer KMS depending on region and contract. We'll include the exact options.

[21:40] Priya Nair: one thing — SSO mapping. we have groups and roles in Okta. how do we map to Redwood RBAC?

[22:00] Lena Park: we accept SAML/SO SAML? sorry, yes SAML and OIDC. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles; we'll share a sample SAML attribute mapping. For pilot, we recommend an "ops" role and a "developer" role to start.

[24:35] Marcus Hsu: also a note on model routing — if Dedicated is constrained, we can fallback to a compatible hosted model variant to keep critical paths serving. it's part of our graceful degradation plan.

[25:55] Samir Patel: fallback is fine but track cost — we don't want surprises. can we get token-level cost breakdowns in console?

[26:20] Lena Park: yes. console has token-cost and latency breakdown per-route/model. we can also turn on alerts for unexpected spend.

[28:00] Anita Gomez: about canary rollouts — we need a canary config for new model versions and automatic rollback. does Redwood support that out of box?

[28:25] Marcus Hsu: yes — canary/A-B and auto-fallback. you can tie rollouts to eval sets and automatic regression thresholds. we recommend starting with a 5% canary.

[30:05] Priya Nair: interesting — can we run a small A/B with our prompt set?

[30:25] Marcus Hsu: absolutely, that's how we validate. we'll help define the baseline metrics.

[32:10] Lena Park: okay back to runbook items — Marcus will run through the staging checklist: VPC CIDR, routes, peering contact, test harness endpoints, cert thumbprints, SSH bastion plan, and a list of test prompts.

[33:40] Marcus Hsu: i'll enumerate: 1) VPC CIDR & peering approval, 2) NSG/ACLs for egress only to Redwood ingestion endpoints, 3) cert chain pin for TLS, 4) SAML metadata for SSO mapping, 5) KMS details if CMK desired, 6) sample traffic profile for pilot sizing.

[36:05] Samir Patel: for the sample traffic, do you need per-minute QPS or token distribution? we can provide both.

[36:25] Marcus Hsu: both help; QPS and average sequence length — that informs kernel selection and batching config.

[38:00] Anita Gomez: we'll share last-quarter traffic from our current inference provider as a baseline.

[39:15] Lena Park: timeline idea — get the staging peering done in week 1, run a network test and smoke inference with a 1k request batch in week 2, then pilot load tests in week 3. Does that align with your timeline?

[39:42] Priya Nair: yes that works. we want pilot active in about three weeks — internal stakeholders ready by then.

[41:05] Samir Patel: any concerns on TLS cert rotation or pinned certs? we handle rotation from our side but want to ensure no downtime in peering.

[41:30] Marcus Hsu: we rotate certs gracefully; we'll share cert rotation procedures. For pinned certs we can support a cert-rotation window.

[43:10] Anita Gomez: curious — any initial recommendations on model family? we currently use a mid-size open model for response generation.

[43:33] Marcus Hsu: based on low-latency needs, a quantized LLM with low-memory kernels often hits the sweet spot. we'll recommend a variant after you share sample prompts.

[45:00] Priya Nair: what's the pilot cost ballpark? rough $/1000 tokens or flat monthly?

[45:20] Lena Park: for hosted it's mainly per-token; for Dedicated it's a commit+usage hybrid. I'll send a small-ball estimate for your QPS profile but note it's preliminary.

[47:05] Samir Patel: security docs — can you send SOC2, penetration test summary, and encryption whitepaper?

[47:22] Lena Park: yes, we'll attach SOC2 and the infosec pack to the runbook link.

[49:00] Marcus Hsu: quick demo point — when we run the staging test we'll capture latency tails and KV cache hit rates; those will guide batch/kv tuning.

[50:15] Anita Gomez: great. any gotchas we should prepare for?

[50:30] Marcus Hsu: minor — if you have very bursty traffic, autoscaling interplay with cache warmup can show higher p95 at start; warmup runs before cutover help. Also watch for prompt length variance which affects kernel paths.

[51:25] Lena Park: recap: Redwood to share runbook, pricing, SOC2 docs; Starlight to provide CIDR, SAML metadata, sample prompts, and traffic profile. Schedule network test next week.

[51:50] Anita Gomez: sounds good, thanks everyone.

[51:55] Priya Nair: thanks all.

[52:00] Lena Park: thanks, bye.

Recap & Next Steps (verbatim):
- Lena: Share onboarding runbook, RBAC mapping examples, SOC2 + security pack, Dedicated pricing estimate (due 2027-09-08/09).
- Samir: Send VPC CIDR, proposed bastion plan, ACL list (due 2027-09-10).
- Marcus & Samir: Schedule staging network test (target week of 2027-09-13).
- Priya: Share prompt sets and evals for rollout baseline (due 2027-09-12).
